# Coding Standards

These rules apply to every change in this codebase, regardless of size.

## Language and module system

- TypeScript `strict: true` — no `any`; use discriminated unions or `unknown` with narrowing
- Bundler module resolution (Vite) — do **not** add `.js` extensions to local imports
  ```ts
  // correct
  import { Foo } from './Foo';
  // wrong
  import { Foo } from './Foo.js';
  ```

## Import order

Order imports from most to least generic:

1. Node.js built-ins (`path`, `fs`, `crypto`)
2. Third-party packages (`react`, `zod`, `express`)
3. Local modules (`./Foo`, `../utils/bar`)

Separate each group with a blank line:

```ts
// correct
import path from 'path';

import { z } from 'zod';

import { MyService } from './MyService';

// wrong — mixed order, no group separation
import { MyService } from './MyService';
import { z } from 'zod';
import path from 'path';
```

---

## Component structure

- Keep components small and focused — one responsibility per component
- Co-locate styles and tests with the component file
  ```
  MyComponent/
    MyComponent.tsx
    MyComponent.css   (or .module.css)
    MyComponent.test.tsx
  ```

## Quality gates

Every change must pass these before committing:

```bash
npm run typecheck   # must produce no errors
npm run lint        # must produce no errors
npm test            # must pass with zero failures
```

Before opening a PR:

```bash
npm run build       # full pipeline — must complete without errors
```

---

## Testing

### File placement and naming

Test files live **next to the source file they test** — not in a separate `__tests__` or `test/` directory. Use suffixes to distinguish test types:

| Suffix | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.test.ts` | Unit tests — fast, no I/O, all dependencies stubbed or injected |
| `.integration-test.ts` | Integration tests — real I/O, real DB, real external services |

```
src/
  projection/
    services/
      RMDService.ts
      RMDService.test.ts
      RMDService.integration-test.ts   # only if integration coverage is needed
```

### Test fixture suites

When a test requires a multi-file support module — a concrete subclass used as a test double, shared wiring helpers, domain-specific types — place it in a `__fixtures__/<name>/` subdirectory co-located with the source it tests:

```
src/
  knowledge/
    psm/
      assessment-psm.ts
      __fixtures__/
        my-domain/
          my-domain-psm.ts         # concrete subclass used as a fixture
          my-domain-psm.test.ts    # test that exercises it end-to-end
          wiring.ts
          types.ts
```

**Build exclusion:** add `**/__fixtures__/**` to the TypeScript `tsconfig.json` `exclude` array so fixture files are never emitted to `dist/` or included in the published package.

**Type-checking:** a separate `tsconfig.test.json` (used only with `--noEmit`) should override `exclude` to omit `**/__fixtures__/**` so fixture support files are still type-checked during development.

**Lint guard:** add a `no-restricted-imports` rule scoped to production source files to prevent any `**/__fixtures__/**` import from leaking into production code.

### Coverage requirements

Every public function, method, or service must have unit tests covering:

- **Happy path** — expected inputs produce the correct output
- **Edge cases** — boundary values, empty collections, zero, `undefined`/`null` where the type permits
- **Error cases** — invalid inputs, thrown exceptions, rejected promises

### Test quality rules

- **Test behaviour, not implementation.** Assert on inputs and outputs, not on internal state or the order of private calls. A test that breaks when you rename a private method is testing the wrong thing.
- **One logical assertion per test.** A test that checks three unrelated things hides which one broke. Split it.
- **Independent tests.** No shared mutable state between tests. Use `beforeEach` to reset any state that must exist before each case.
- **Descriptive names.** The test name should read as a plain-English sentence describing what is true: `'returns undefined when balance is zero'`, not `'test 1'` or `'works'`.
- **Arrange – Act – Assert.** Structure each test in three clear stages: set up inputs, invoke the subject, assert the result. A blank line between stages aids readability.

### Shared helpers

Test factory functions (`makeAsset`, `makeContext`, etc.) that appear in more than one test file must be extracted to a shared helper module co-located with the subject under test. Test code is production code — the same duplication and quality rules apply.

---

## No duplication

Any code pattern repeated more than twice must be extracted:

- **Pure logic** → a standalone function
- **Stateful or object-bound logic** → a class method
- **Cross-module utility** → a shared module

This applies equally to test code and production code.

---

## Prefer interfaces

When more than one class implements the same behavioural contract, extract a named interface. Calling code — constructor parameters, function signatures, service dependencies — must accept the interface type, never the concrete class. A second implementation appearing is the signal to extract; do not wait for a third.

---

## Naming

Names express *what*, not *how*. A good name makes a comment unnecessary.

- Booleans read as predicates: `isRetired`, `hasBalance`, `budgetMet`
- No abbreviations except universally recognised ones (`id`, `url`, `ctx`, `amt`)
- Avoid generic names: `data`, `info`, `manager`, `helper`, `utils` — name the concept instead

---

## Comments

Only write a comment when the **why** behind the code would surprise a future reader: a hidden constraint, a subtle invariant, a workaround for a specific bug. Do not describe what the code does — well-named identifiers already do that. If removing the comment would not confuse anyone, do not write it.

---

## No magic literals

Inline numbers and strings that carry business meaning must be named constants:

```ts
// wrong
const ceiling = 383900 * Math.pow(1.025, years);

// correct
const BRACKET_24_MFJ_2024 = 383900;
const BRACKET_INFLATION = 0.025;
const ceiling = BRACKET_24_MFJ_2024 * Math.pow(1 + BRACKET_INFLATION, years);
```

---

## Dependency injection

Services receive their dependencies through the constructor — they do not instantiate dependencies internally. Constructor parameters are typed as interfaces, not concrete classes. This keeps every unit testable in isolation without touching real implementations.

---

## Pure functions

Prefer functions that take inputs and return outputs with no side effects. Mutations and I/O belong at the outermost layer of the application. Pure code is trivially testable and composable.

---

## File size

A file exceeding ~300 lines is a signal — not a hard rule — that it has taken on more than one responsibility. Treat it as a prompt to revisit the design and consider splitting.
